name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MATCHLIST_Q01 - SI base quantities and their base units

questiontext.text:
Match List I (SI Base Quantity) with List II (SI Base Unit):

List I List II
A. Electric currentI. kelvin
B. Thermodynamic temperatureII. mole
C. Amount of substanceIII. candela
D. Luminous intensityIV. ampere

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of the unit of electric current
Electric current is an SI base quantity defined with the base unit ampere (symbol: \(\text{A}\)).

Step 2: Identification of the unit of thermodynamic temperature
Thermodynamic temperature is an SI base quantity defined with the base unit kelvin (symbol: \(\text{K}\)).

Step 3: Identification of the unit of amount of substance
Amount of substance is an SI base quantity containing elementary entities, defined with the base unit mole (symbol: \(\text{mol}\)).

Step 4: Identification of the unit of luminous intensity
Luminous intensity is an SI base quantity defined with the base unit candela (symbol: \(\text{cd}\)).

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs electric current with ampere, thermodynamic temperature with kelvin, amount of substance with mole, and luminous intensity with candela.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MATCHLIST_Q02 - Units retained for general use and SI equivalents

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Unit retained for general use) with List II (Value in SI unit):

List I List II
A. 1 quintalI. \(10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\)
B. 1 hectareII. \(10^2\text{ kg}\)
C. 1 barIII. \(10^4\text{ m}^2\)
D. 1 litreIV. \(10^5\text{ Pa}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: SI equivalent of quintal
A quintal is a metric unit of mass retained for general use and equals \(100\text{ kg} = 10^2\text{ kg}\).

Step 2: SI equivalent of hectare
A hectare is a unit of land area equal to the area of a square with sides of \(1\text{ hm} = 100\text{ m}\), giving \((100\text{ m})^2 = 10^4\text{ m}^2\).

Step 3: SI equivalent of bar
The bar is a metric unit of pressure defined as \(0.1\text{ MPa} = 10^5\text{ Pa}\).

Step 4: SI equivalent of litre
The litre is a unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre: \(1\text{ dm}^3 = (10^{-1}\text{ m})^3 = 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\).

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs quintal with \(10^2\text{ kg}\), hectare with \(10^4\text{ m}^2\), bar with \(10^5\text{ Pa}\), and litre with \(10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MATCHLIST_Q03 - Number of significant figures in measured values

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Measured value) with List II (Number of significant figures):

List I List II
A. \(0.005\text{ m}\)I. 3
B. \(4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)II. 1
C. \(2.64 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}\)III. 4
D. \(0.2370\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)IV. 2

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Significant figures in \(0.005\text{ m}\)
For a number less than \(1\), zeros to the right of the decimal point but to the left of the first non-zero digit are not significant. Only the non-zero digit \(5\) is significant, giving \(1\) significant figure.

Step 2: Significant figures in \(4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)
All non-zero digits are significant. The digits \(4\) and \(8\) are both significant, giving \(2\) significant figures.

Step 3: Significant figures in \(2.64 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}\)
In scientific notation, the power of \(10\) is irrelevant to the count of significant figures; all digits in the base number are significant. The digits \(2, 6, 4\) yield \(3\) significant figures.

Step 4: Significant figures in \(0.2370\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)
The leading zero before the decimal is not significant. The digits \(2, 3, 7\) are significant, and trailing zeros in a number with a decimal point are significant. Thus, the four digits \(2, 3, 7, 0\) give \(4\) significant figures.

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs \(0.005\text{ m}\) with \(1\) significant figure, \(4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) with \(2\) significant figures, \(2.64 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}\) with \(3\) significant figures, and \(0.2370\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) with \(4\) significant figures.

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Physical quantity) with List II (Dimensional formula):

List I List II
A. Universal gravitational constant (\(G\))I. \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]\)
B. Planck constant (\(h\))II. \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\)
C. ForceIII. \([\text{M L}\text{T}^{-2}]\)
D. Kinetic energyIV. \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Dimensional formula of universal gravitational constant
From Newton's law of gravitation, \(F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}\), so \(G = \frac{F r^2}{m_1 m_2}\). Substituting dimensions gives \([G] = \frac{[\text{M L T}^{-2}][\text{L}^2]}{[\text{M}][\text{M}]} = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\).

Step 2: Dimensional formula of Planck constant
From the energy relation \(E = h \nu\), the Planck constant is \(h = \frac{E}{\nu}\). Substituting dimensions gives \([h] = \frac{[\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]}{[\text{T}^{-1}]} = [\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]\).

Step 3: Dimensional formula of force
Force is mass times acceleration: \([F] = [\text{M}][\text{L T}^{-2}] = [\text{M L T}^{-2}]\).

Step 4: Dimensional formula of kinetic energy
Kinetic energy is given by \(K = \frac{1}{2}m v^2\). Substituting dimensions gives \([K] = [\text{M}][\text{L T}^{-1}]^2 = [\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\).

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs the universal gravitational constant with \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\), the Planck constant with \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]\), force with \([\text{M L T}^{-2}]\), and kinetic energy with \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\).
